title: TimeFlowCodec: An Orthogonal Video Coding Architecture for Screen and Synthetic Content via Per-Pixel Temporal Regression
description: Modern video coding standards (H.264/AVC, H.265/HEVC, AV1, and H.266/VVC) rely on the canonical hybrid model: spatial block partitioning, 2D Discrete Cosine/Sine Transforms (DCT/DST), and 4:2:0 chroma subsampling. While near-optimal for band-limited natural camera footage, these foundational assumptions break down on synthetic screen content, including software user interfaces, terminal consoles, vector presentations, and digital animation. Sharp graphical boundaries and single-pixel text stems represent mathematical step discontinuities; transforming these structures with truncated 2D Fourier-basis transforms induces severe Gibbs ringing (mosquito noise), while 4:2:0 chroma decimation obliterates syntax highlighting and colored typography. We present TimeFlowCodec (TFC), a video compression architecture that eliminates spatial block transforms in favor of direct 1D per-pixel temporal regression. By modeling the intensity evolution of each pixel over discrete temporal windows using closed-form Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression, TFC preserves native 4:4:4 spatial edge fidelity with zero spatial ringing. The resulting bitstream eliminates inter-block spatial dependencies, enabling O(1) working memory state per pixel and highly vectorizable parallel decoding. We outline the theoretical formulation, container specification, and experimental evaluation methodology against standard hybrid codecs.
notes: Preprint manuscript describing the TimeFlowCodec video compression architecture, mathematical formulation, streaming container specification, and empirical JVET-SCC rate-distortion benchmarks.
